title: JSON Lines trace for one agent loop step
description: This example shows how to emit a structured trace for a single perceive-plan-act loop step, writing one JSON object per line to a file that can be searched and appended indefinitely.

steps.description: Imports and setup: TRACE_PATH is the output file, TRACE_ID groups events from one task.
The demo removes any existing trace file so each run starts fresh. A real agent would only append.
log_event appends one JSON line with a timestamp, trace_id, step number, phase, and any extra fields. This is the core logging function.
Every event gets the same trace_id and step number, so all three phases of one loop step can be queried together.
fake_llm stands in for a model call. It returns a tool call decision with token counts and a finish_reason. Changing finish_reason to 'length' shows how the trace captures the difference.
fake_tool simulates a search tool that returns a factual answer about Ursinus College's founding.
The perceive phase hashes the question instead of storing it, logs the hash and estimated prompt tokens.
The plan phase calls fake_llm, measures latency, and logs the model name, token counts, finish_reason, and the decision to call a tool.
The act phase calls fake_tool, then logs the tool name, success, result size, and the rule that authorized the action (CHARTER.md#cite-before-claim).

steps.question: What three lines appear in the trace file after one loop step?
steps.answer: One line for perceive with the query hash, one for plan with the model call details, and one for act with the tool result and the governing rule.

steps.description: The perceive event is logged with the question hash (12fb6d74) and estimated prompt tokens (15).
The plan event is logged: model hermes-3, 0ms latency, 15 prompt tokens, 9 completion tokens, finish_reason stop, decision tool_call to search.
The act event is logged: search tool succeeded, 66 result characters, rule CHARTER.md#cite-before-claim. The answer and full trace are then printed.
